text:
Every Lightning game this season comes with an asterisk the size of Nikita Kucherov. The franchise's all-time leading scorer asked for a trade at the end of October, saying publicly it was about "poor communication and respect" rather than money, and Andrei Vasilevskiy told TSN he hopes "that something will change." Meanwhile Kucherov keeps producing, including an overtime winner in Minnesota on Saturday.

What makes it strange is that the team is good. Tampa Bay is 11-4-2 with 24 points and 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and the results match the process. The surprise engine has been the checking line: Zemgus Girgensons, Pontus Holmberg and Ilya Mikheyev have outscored teams 10-3 with 61% of the chances, and Ryan McDonagh and Erik Cernak are 14-5 together. Charle-Edouard D'Astous (10 points in 10) and Holmberg (9 in 10) are running above their chances, so expect some cooling there.

The new worry is Brayden Point, who left Sunday's game in Winnipeg early and, per Jon Cooper, might miss some time. The Kucherov, Point and Jake Guentzel line has been dominant (8-2 in goals), and losing two-thirds of it in different ways would test a lineup that has looked deep. Our simulations still make them a 91% playoff team projecting about 105 points. The thing to watch isn't the standings. It's the phone.
